content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Today increasing importance is being attached to cultivating college student team spirit." You can make statements, give reasons, or cite examples to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

modelEssay.title: Cultivating College Student Team Spirit
modelEssay.content: Today increasing importance is being attached to cultivating college student team spirit. This trend is not only necessary but also vital for the holistic development of students. Firstly, teamwork fosters a sense of belonging and cooperation, which are essential in both academic and professional settings. Students who work in teams learn to communicate effectively, respect diverse opinions, and solve problems collectively. Moreover, engaging in group activities helps students to develop leadership skills and enhances their ability to work under pressure. These skills are indispensable in today's competitive job market. In conclusion, nurturing team spirit among college students is crucial for their future success. It not only prepares them for the challenges of the modern workplace but also instills a sense of community and shared responsibility.

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话1。

transcript.text: Welcome to the Book Club.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 欢迎来到图书俱乐部。

transcript.text: Today's guest is Susan Lane, the author of a new book on personal finances that has already sold half a million copies.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今天的嘉宾是苏珊·莱恩，她是一本关于个人理财的新书的作者，该书已售出50万册。

transcript.text: Hi, Susan.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗨，苏珊。

transcript.text: Your book is extremely successful.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你的书非常成功。

transcript.text: Why do you think that is?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你认为这是为什么？

transcript.text: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我认为这是因为我的信息，即把幸福置于金钱之上作为优先事项。

transcript.text: So many of us in my generation have spent decades trying to earn more money just to consume more, but it made us more miserable.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们这一代的许多人花了几十年试图赚更多的钱只是为了消费更多，但这让我们更加痛苦。

transcript.text: You yourself were once caught in that cycle, working for two decades as an executive and earning a high salary, but still accumulating debt.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你自己也曾陷入那种循环，担任高管工作了二十年，拿着高薪，但仍在积累债务。

transcript.text: I most certainly was.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我绝对是。

transcript.text: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我赚了数百万，但四年前我辞职成为作家时，我欠了超过3万美元。

transcript.text: So how did you escape that pattern, and what would you advise other people to do?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么你是如何摆脱那种模式的，你会建议其他人做什么？

transcript.text: The first change is in what we value.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 第一个变化是在我们重视什么方面。

transcript.text: We need to emphasize things that actually make us happy, like relationships, the environment, or even our hobbies.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们需要强调那些真正让我们快乐的事情，比如人际关系、环境，甚至我们的爱好。

transcript.text: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change, and so will our financial behavior.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 一旦我们把正确的事情作为优先事项，我们的目标就会改变，我们的财务行为也会随之改变。

transcript.text: How does that translate into practical action?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那如何转化为实际行动？

transcript.text: Can you give our audience examples of what you're talking about on an everyday basis?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你能给我们的听众举一些你所说的日常例子吗？

transcript.text: The major areas for action are usually housing, food, and transportation.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 行动的主要领域通常是住房、食物和交通。

transcript.text: So, people might share a home with friends instead of living on their own, bring lunch from home instead of going to restaurants, and use public transport instead of owning a car.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以，人们可能和朋友合住而不是独自居住，自带午餐而不是去餐馆，使用公共交通而不是拥有汽车。

transcript.text: Those sound like major sacrifices.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那些听起来像是重大的牺牲。

transcript.text: I could never share my home.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我永远无法分享我的家。

transcript.text: I need my own space.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我需要自己的空间。

transcript.text: But they aren't sacrifices.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但它们不是牺牲。

transcript.text: When people change their values, their desires change.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当人们改变价值观时，他们的欲望也会改变。

transcript.text: So in the example of housing, if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space, but giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以在住房的例子中，如果我们重视人际关系，合住不是剥夺自己的空间，而是给我们一个与所爱之人共度更多时光的机会。

transcript.text: Indeed it is.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 确实如此。

transcript.text: Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 克里斯托弗，谢谢你邀请我来画廊。

transcript.text: I haven't visited here since your predecessor's retirement function.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: Would you like to see the newest additions to our collection first, Catherine?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 凯瑟琳，你想先看看我们收藏的新品吗？

transcript.text: Are those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那些是丹妮尔·格雷戈里的风景画吗？

transcript.text: I absolutely adore her work.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我非常喜欢她的作品。

transcript.text: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it's quite exquisite.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这第一件作品是艺术家本人送给画廊的礼物，非常精致。

transcript.text: I love how she depicts the barren landscape.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我喜欢她描绘荒芜风景的方式。

transcript.text: The colors complement each other perfectly.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 色彩完美地相互衬托。

transcript.text: You can sense the desolation in the picture.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你能感受到画中的荒凉。

transcript.text: This piece was inspired by Gregory's recent trek in the Gobi Desert.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这件作品灵感来自格雷戈里最近在戈壁沙漠的徒步旅行。

transcript.text: And how did you obtain her other piece over here?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那你们是怎么得到她这边的另一件作品的？

transcript.text: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector, who lent it to the gallery for display.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它被一位匿名收藏家在拍卖会上购得，并借给画廊展出。

transcript.text: This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这幅作品是她最受赞誉的画作之一。

transcript.text: It must have cost that collector a small fortune to purchase this.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那位收藏家买下它一定花了一大笔钱。

transcript.text: Obviously.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 显然。

transcript.text: I can't disclose the exact amount he paid, but it was substantial.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我不能透露他支付的确切金额，但数目不小。

transcript.text: There's so much detail in this painting.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这幅画中有如此多的细节。

transcript.text: I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我感觉我真的能沉浸在场景中。

transcript.text: I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我特别喜欢山在湖中倒影所创造的对称性。

transcript.text: This particular piece was the one that was nominated for a Gateway Award.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这件特定的作品是被提名Gateway奖的那一件。

transcript.text: I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony as Gregory's guest.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我很幸运能作为格雷戈里的客人出席颁奖典礼。

transcript.text: So, you know her personally.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以，你本人认识她。

transcript.text: I assume she's an eccentric artist.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我猜她是个古怪的艺术家。

transcript.text: Quite the opposite, in fact.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 事实上，恰恰相反。

transcript.text: She's not at all eccentric.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 她一点也不古怪。

transcript.text: I would say she's one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我会说她是我认识的最随和、最聪明的人之一。

transcript.text: I'd love to be able to meet her.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我很想能见到她。

transcript.text: There are so many questions I'd like to ask.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: What a coincidence.

transcript.translation: 真是巧啊。

transcript.text: I'm meeting her for dinner tonight.

transcript.text: Would you like to come along?

transcript.text: I'd love to.

transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 文章1。

transcript.text: Forgiveness is the release of resentment or anger.
transcript.translation: 宽恕是释放怨恨或愤怒。

transcript.text: Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation.
transcript.translation: 宽恕并不意味着和解。

transcript.text: We don't have to return to the same relationship, nor do we have to accept the same harmful behaviors from an offender.
transcript.translation: 我们不必回到原来的关系，也不必接受冒犯者同样的有害行为。

transcript.text: Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims.
transcript.translation: 宽恕对某些受害者的心理健康至关重要。

transcript.text: It propels people forward rather than keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma.
transcript.translation: 它推动人们前进，而不是让他们情感上纠结于不公或创伤。

transcript.text: Carrying the hurt or anger of an offense leads the body to release stress chemicals.
transcript.translation: 携带冒犯带来的伤害或愤怒会导致身体释放应激化学物质。

transcript.text: Eliminating the perpetual flow of those chemicals may also explain why forgiveness provides physical health benefits.
transcript.translation: 消除这些化学物质的持续流动也可能解释为什么宽恕能带来身体健康益处。

transcript.text: There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course.
transcript.translation: 有些情况下，宽恕并非最佳选择。

transcript.text: Sometimes a victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive.
transcript.translation: 有时，当受害者允许自己不宽恕时，他们会变得更加强大。

transcript.text: Forgiveness can be challenging.
transcript.translation: 宽恕可能具有挑战性。

transcript.text: This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all.
transcript.translation: 当冒犯方提供不真诚的道歉，或者根本没有道歉时，尤其如此。

transcript.text: However, it's often the healthiest path forward.
transcript.translation: 然而，它通常是最健康的发展路径。

transcript.text: It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender.
transcript.translation: 通过培养对冒犯者的同情来培养宽恕是很重要的。

transcript.text: Reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.
transcript.translation: 反思该行为是出于恶意，还是由冒犯者生活中的困境所引起。

transcript.text: What about forgiving ourselves?
transcript.translation: 那么原谅我们自己呢？

transcript.text: We sometimes need to take responsibility for mistakes, but intense guilt and shame aren't a desirable outcome in the long run.
transcript.translation: 我们有时需要为错误承担责任，但从长远来看，强烈的内疚和羞耻并非理想结果。

transcript.text: Forgiving yourself may seem like an ambiguous process.
transcript.translation: 原谅自己可能看起来像是一个模糊的过程。

transcript.text: You can begin by acknowledging that you are at fault.
transcript.translation: 你可以从承认自己有过错开始。

transcript.text: Take responsibility for the hurt you caused.
transcript.translation: 为你所造成的伤害承担责任。

transcript.text: Then, reflect on why the event occurred.
transcript.translation: 然后，反思事件发生的原因。

transcript.text: Draw the lessons you learned and try to avoid committing a similar offense in the future.
transcript.translation: 吸取教训，并努力避免将来犯下类似的过错。

transcript.text: The Glasgow Subway first opened in 1896 as a cable-hauled system.
transcript.translation: 格拉斯哥地铁于1896年首次开通，是一个缆索牵引系统。

transcript.text: It is generally recognized as the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest.
transcript.translation: 它被普遍认为是继伦敦和布达佩斯之后的世界第三条地下铁路。

transcript.text: In its long history, it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations.
transcript.translation: 在其悠久的历史中，它从未被扩建，始终保持为一条仅有15个车站的单环线。

transcript.text: At its peak, it served the shipyard workers on the south side of the city.
transcript.translation: 在鼎盛时期，它服务于城市南侧的造船厂工人。

transcript.text: In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry, and the popularity of private transport grew.
transcript.translation: 在20世纪60年代，造船业出现衰退，私人交通工具的普及率上升。

transcript.text: As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership.
transcript.translation: 因此，地铁的乘客量急剧下降。

transcript.text: It ran with little further change until 1977, when its new operators closed it for major modernization investment.
transcript.translation: 它一直运行，几乎没有进一步变化，直到1977年，新运营商将其关闭以进行重大现代化投资。

transcript.text: Carriages were replaced, ventilation was improved, and the main depot was also renovated and fitted with connecting tracks to replace the outdated crane transfer mechanism.
transcript.translation: 车厢被更换，通风得到改善，主车辆段也进行了翻新，并安装了连接轨道以取代过时的起重机转运机制。

transcript.text: The subway in its present form reopened for operation in April 1980.
transcript.translation: 现行的地铁于1980年4月重新开放运营。

transcript.text: Since its relaunch, the subway has seen a revival in its fortunes.
transcript.translation: 自重新启动以来，地铁的命运有所复苏。

transcript.text: It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city centre.
transcript.translation: 它作为其他交通方式的可行替代品，并在缓解市中心交通拥堵方面发挥了重要作用。

transcript.text: In 1996, the system reached an important milestone, 100 years.
transcript.translation: 1996年，该系统达到了一个重要里程碑，即100周年。

transcript.text: To commemorate this special event, the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated.
transcript.translation: 为了纪念这一特殊事件，列车车厢的配色方案得到了更新。

transcript.text: Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations.
transcript.translation: 最近，高科技系统如智能卡售票机和智能闸门在所有地铁站得到应用。

transcript.text: The smart card provides more convenient travel, and passengers simply top up their cards and tap them to get in and out the subway.
transcript.translation: 智能卡提供了更便捷的出行，乘客只需充值卡片并刷卡进出地铁。

transcript.text: Since its launch, the technology has been adopted by more than 100,000 subway customers.
transcript.translation: 自推出以来，该技术已被超过10万地铁乘客采用。

transcript.text: If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else.
transcript.translation: 如果你参观大烟山国家公园，你最可能记住的是路边或营地的熊。

transcript.text: Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks.
transcript.translation: 熊是我们许多国家公园中最受欢迎的动物。

transcript.text: In these mountains, where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer.
transcript.translation: 在这些山中，熊的数量达到数百只，夏季观察这些大型野生动物的机会很多。

transcript.text: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans.
transcript.translation: 由于国家公园是野生动物保护区，不允许打扰本土动物，多年的保护已使野熊对人类的恐惧逐渐消失。

transcript.text: Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds.
transcript.translation: 现在，许多熊不再依赖自身资源谋生，而是巡逻公园道路和营地。

transcript.text: They give the garbage cans a frequent going-over.
transcript.translation: 它们频繁地翻找垃圾桶。

transcript.text: An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them.
transcript.translation: 公园游客偶尔提供的食物，这是一种非法且危险的行为，使它们变成了乞丐。

transcript.text: Bears are very often hungry, and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable.
transcript.translation: 熊经常饥饿，而且由于它们几乎以任何植物或动物为食，垃圾也是完全可以接受的。

transcript.text: Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone and, consequently, trouble could lie ahead.
transcript.translation: 然而，喂养它们代表了一种被误导的善意，因为熊会开始期望每个人如此慷慨，因此，麻烦可能就在眼前。

transcript.text: Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.
transcript.translation: 公园规则禁止喂熊。

transcript.text: Violators are arrested.
transcript.translation: 违规者将被逮捕。

transcript.text: Every year, doctors who have offices near the park treat a number of cases of bear bites and bear scratches.
transcript.translation: 每年，公园附近诊所的医生治疗许多熊咬伤和熊抓伤病例。

transcript.text: Some of the accidents have come about in strange ways.
transcript.translation: 一些事故以奇怪的方式发生。

transcript.text: One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs when the mother bear appeared and insisted upon having some of the food.
transcript.translation: 一名男子正在喂两只小熊崽时，母熊出现并坚持要一些食物。

transcript.text: Shoving the big bear aside with one hand, the man continued feeding the cubs when suddenly he was struck a fierce blow in the face.
transcript.translation: 男子用一只手将大熊推开，继续喂小熊崽，突然他脸上被狠狠打了一击。

transcript.text: A bear, prompted by the food that a lady kept offering to him, entered the car where the generous person was sitting.
transcript.translation: 一只熊，由于一位女士不断向它提供食物，进入了这位慷慨人士所在的汽车。

transcript.text: Her efforts to push the bear out of the car resulted in injuries.
transcript.translation: 她试图将熊推出车外的努力导致受伤。

transcript.text: A man required medical attention after he applied a lighted cigarette to a bear's nose.
transcript.translation: 一名男子在将点燃的香烟按在熊鼻子上后需要医疗救治。

transcript.text: Another man tried to boost a bear into the front seat of his car so that he might take a picture of a bear sitting beside his wife who was behind the wheel.
transcript.translation: 另一名男子试图将熊推进汽车前座，以便拍摄一张熊坐在他妻子（驾驶员）旁边的照片。

transcript.text: Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small.
transcript.translation: 由于熊更喜欢道路和营地，徒步旅行者在公园小径上遇到熊的可能性很小。

transcript.text: But there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar.
transcript.translation: 但机会总是有的，因为熊似乎知道你是否带了午餐或糖果棒。

transcript.text: He may even insist on taking it.
transcript.translation: 它甚至可能坚持要拿走它。

transcript.text: Why do we form opinions or attitudes about someone or something without really knowing much about them?
transcript.translation: 为什么我们会在不真正了解某人或某事的情况下，就对其形成观点或态度？

transcript.text: Just hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions positively or negatively.
transcript.translation: 仅仅听到关于某个人、地方或事物的好坏，就能正面或负面地影响我们的观点。

transcript.text: But letting the opinions of another person determine what our opinions will be is dangerous.
transcript.translation: 但让另一个人的观点来决定我们的观点，这是危险的。

transcript.text: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice.
transcript.translation: 在真正了解某人或某事之前就形成看法，被称为偏见。

transcript.text: Pre- means before and judice refers to judgment.
transcript.translation: "Pre-" 意为之前，"judice" 指的是判断。

transcript.text: Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.
transcript.translation: 因此，偏见意为在没有充分了解之前就做出判断。

transcript.text: We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something.
transcript.translation: 我们可能对某人或某事怀有偏见（赞成或反对）。

transcript.text: In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture.
transcript.translation: 无论是哪种情况，我们只允许自己看到画面的一半。

transcript.text: Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad.
transcript.translation: 这个世界上很少有人或事物是完全好或完全坏的。

transcript.text: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths, or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.
transcript.translation: 带有偏见的态度通常基于谣言、半真半假的信息或错误的信息，它们是危险的，因为会阻碍我们了解某人或某事的真相。

transcript.text: People form prejudices against others for many reasons.
transcript.translation: 人们形成对他人的偏见有很多原因。

transcript.text: Differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation.
transcript.translation: 种族、宗教、性别或职业上的差异。

transcript.text: Prejudices keep people apart.
transcript.translation: 偏见使人与人之间产生隔阂。

transcript.text: They keep us from really knowing and understanding each other.
transcript.translation: 它们阻碍我们真正了解和理解彼此。

transcript.text: We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent.
transcript.translation: 我们应该为自己是谁以及所代表的群体感到自豪。

transcript.text: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.
transcript.translation: 然而，当自豪感开始转变为优越感，即当我们认为自己的群体或信仰比周围人更好时，我们便开始形成可能有害的偏见态度。

transcript.text: For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion.
transcript.translation: 例如，一个群体的偏见态度可能阻止另一个群体进入某些学校、住在他们想要的任何社区、或者获得工作或晋升。

transcript.text: Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people.
transcript.translation: 极端的偏见情绪已导致无辜者的死亡。

transcript.text: We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions.
transcript.translation: 我们对自己的想法和观点负责。

transcript.text: When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.
transcript.translation: 当我们让别人告诉我们该如何看待某人或某事时，我们便放弃了对自己生活的部分掌控。

transcript.text: Before you form an attitude or opinion, find out for yourself about the person or the thing in question.
transcript.translation: 在你形成某种态度或观点之前，自己去了解相关的人或事物。

transcript.text: Sometimes we don't realize that we hold prejudiced attitudes toward or against someone or something.
transcript.translation: 有时我们没有意识到自己对某人或某事怀有偏见态度（赞成或反对）。

transcript.text: We need to carefully examine our lives and our fears, and to ask ourselves whether our attitudes come from our personal knowledge and experience or from rumors and fear of the unknown.
transcript.translation: 我们需要仔细审视自己的生活和恐惧，并问问自己，我们的态度是来自个人的知识和经验，还是来自谣言和对未知的恐惧。

transcript.text: The good news about prejudice is that we are not born with it.
transcript.translation: 关于偏见的一个好消息是，我们并非生来就有它。

transcript.text: Prejudiced attitudes and opinions develop over time.
transcript.translation: 带有偏见的态度和观点是随时间发展的。

transcript.text: But with education and knowledge, we can replace our prejudices with cooperation and understanding.
transcript.translation: 但通过教育和知识，我们可以用合作与理解来取代我们的偏见。

transcript.text: Recording 3.
transcript.translation: 录音3。

transcript.text: When I started high school, it was a shock.
transcript.translation: 当我开始上高中时，那是一个冲击。

transcript.text: I had spent 8 years fighting my way to be the most popular kid in the Catholic school student body.
transcript.translation: 我花了8年时间努力成为天主教学校学生群体中最受欢迎的孩子。

transcript.text: I had been a big, tough 8th grader, and suddenly I was a lowly 9th grader bullied by the big, tough 12th grade seniors who ran the high school.
transcript.translation: 我曾是一个高大强壮的八年级学生，突然间我成了一个卑微的九年级学生，被那些掌管高中、高大强壮的十二年级学长欺凌。

transcript.text: I realized then that it's nice to strive for something, but that you also have to enjoy the moment you're in and be happy where you are.
transcript.translation: 那时我意识到，努力追求某事是好的，但你也必须享受当下，并为所在之处感到快乐。

transcript.text: Rock and roll had always been an important part of my life.
transcript.translation: 摇滚乐一直是我生活中的重要部分。

transcript.text: I remember my friends and I used to drive around until the late hours of the nights listening to the music of rock and roll legends.
transcript.translation: 我记得我和朋友们常常开车四处转，直到深夜，听着摇滚传奇的音乐。

transcript.text: During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime.
transcript.translation: 在那些青少年时期，我建立了我以为会持续一生的友谊。

transcript.text: Most people that age think the same thing, but people drift apart.
transcript.translation: 大多数那个年龄的人都这么想，但人们会渐行渐远。

transcript.text: Jobs, families, and tragedies separate people from those lasting friendships.
transcript.translation: 工作、家庭和悲剧将人们与那些持久的友谊分开。

transcript.text: The tragedy that separated me from my friends forever was the Vietnam War.
transcript.translation: 将我永远与朋友们分开的悲剧是越南战争。

transcript.text: A year after I graduated from high school, I left for Vietnam.
transcript.translation: 高中毕业后一年，我前往越南。

transcript.text: I came back burned out and tired, as though I had lived 10 lifetimes in the short span of 14 months.
transcript.translation: 我回来时筋疲力尽，仿佛在短短14个月内活了10辈子。

transcript.text: The 14 months I was in the war, I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school.
transcript.translation: 在战争中的14个月里，我无法与高中时的朋友们产生共鸣。

transcript.text: They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me.
transcript.translation: 他们仍然显得幼稚，关心那些对我不重要的幼稚事情。

transcript.text: I was still trying to cope with the death, destruction, and evil I had seen in Vietnam.
transcript.translation: 我仍在试图应对在越南所见的死亡、破坏和邪恶。

transcript.text: I felt like we had done terrible things to innocent people there, and in turn, I had seen terrible things done to my friends.
transcript.translation: 我觉得我们在那里对无辜的人做了可怕的事情，反过来，我也看到可怕的事情发生在我的朋友们身上。

transcript.text: I withdrew from my friends and started college.
transcript.translation: 我退出朋友们的生活，开始上大学。

transcript.text: Then I quit college and took many different jobs.
transcript.translation: 然后我退学，做了许多不同的工作。

transcript.text: I spent a lot of my time and money on alcohol and other drugs.
transcript.translation: 我把很多时间和金钱花在酒精和其他毒品上。

transcript.text: Finally, in an effort to get my life going in the right direction again, I sold everything and took what little money I had and bought myself an airplane ticket to Israel.
transcript.translation: 最后，为了让我的人生重回正轨，我卖掉了所有东西，用仅有的一点钱给自己买了一张去以色列的机票。

transcript.text: I went there to study history.
transcript.translation: 我去那里学习历史。

transcript.text: While studying at Haifa University, I met my wife, who was also an American student.
transcript.translation: 在海法大学学习时，我遇到了我的妻子，她也是一名美国学生。

transcript.text: I now teach in a high school back in America.
transcript.translation: 我现在在美国的一所高中教书。

transcript.text: I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago.
transcript.translation: 我看着我的学生，看到他们正在与我多年前挣扎过的许多同样的事情作斗争。

transcript.text: As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.
transcript.translation: 作为一名教师，我尽力帮助他们克服困难。

transcript.text: Questions 23 to 25 are based on the lecture you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题23至25基于你刚刚听到的讲座。

transcript.text: Question 22. How did the speaker feel when he started high school?
transcript.translation: 问题22. 演讲者开始上高中时感觉如何？

transcript.text: Question 23. What did the speaker once think of teenage friendships?
transcript.translation: 问题23. 演讲者曾经如何看待青少年友谊？

transcript.text: Question 24. What do we learn about the speaker when he returned from the Vietnam War?
transcript.translation: 问题24. 当演讲者从越南战争回来时，我们了解到什么？

transcript.text: Question 25. What does the speaker try to do as a teacher? That's the end of Listening Comprehension.
transcript.translation: 问题25. 演讲者作为教师试图做什么？听力理解结束。

paragraphs.text: All 57 schools that were burning coal in 2008 are using less now, and 20 have __27__ coal completely, EIA found.

paragraphs.text: The Sierra Club's Beyond Coal campaign, which also leads campaigns for universities to withdraw their __33__ in coal and other fossil fuels, lists 22 schools that have pledged to move "beyond coal," including Clemson University, Indiana University, Ohio University, Penn State University, the University of Louisville and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

questionGroups.title: Classical music aims to evolve, build audiences without alienating old guard

material.title: Classical music aims to evolve, build audiences without alienating old guard

paragraphs.text: In 1913, classical music sparked a riot in Paris. Igor Stravinsky was introducing his revolutionary "Rite of Spring" ballet to the world, with its discordant melodies and unorthodox choreography (编舞), and the purists in the crowd expressed their disapproval loud and clear. It might have been classical music's version of the time Bob Dylan went electric at the Newport Folk Festival. "The noise, fighting, and shouting in the audience got so loud," NPR's music reporter Miles Hoffman said of the Stravinsky debut, "that the choreographer had to shout out the numbers to the dancers so that they knew what they were supposed to do."
paragraphs.translation: 1913年，古典音乐在巴黎引发了一场骚乱。伊戈尔·斯特拉文斯基向世界介绍了他革命性的芭蕾舞剧《春之祭》，其中不和谐的旋律和非正统的编舞（编舞）引得观众中的纯粹主义者们明确表达了不满。这也许是古典音乐版本的鲍勃·迪伦在纽波特民谣音乐节上改用电吉他的事件。NPR音乐记者迈尔斯·霍夫曼在谈到斯特拉文斯基的首演时说：“观众中的噪音、打斗和喊叫声越来越大，编舞不得不大声喊出节拍数字，好让舞者知道该做什么。”

paragraphs.text: It's difficult to imagine a similar disturbance occurring today within America's sacred symphony halls. In fact, it's hard to picture any kind of disruptive activity at all (unless someone's cell phone happens to go off, and then you'd better watch your back). A mannerly aura (氛围) hangs over most classical proceedings, and many of the genre's biggest supporters would have it no other way.
paragraphs.translation: 很难想象今天在美国神圣的音乐厅里会发生类似的骚动。事实上，很难想象任何具有破坏性的活动（除非有人的手机碰巧响了，那你最好小心点）。礼貌的氛围笼罩着大多数古典音乐活动，而该流派的许多最大支持者也更愿意如此。

paragraphs.text: Today, Western audiences for classical music and opera and ballet are almost always well dressed, older, respectful, achingly silent and often very wealthy (one has to be able to afford most tickets). But as many of America's most storied "highbrow" (高雅的) institutions struggle financially -- the Philadelphia Orchestra's much-publicized rebound from bankruptcy is just one recent example -- classical music fans and theorists are wondering how the medium can weave itself into the 21st century's cultural fabric without sacrificing its integrity.
paragraphs.translation: 如今，西方古典音乐、歌剧和芭蕾舞的观众几乎总是衣着得体、年龄较大、彬彬有礼、极其安静且通常非常富有（必须能负担得起大多数门票）。但随着美国许多最负盛名的“高雅”（高雅的）机构在财务上挣扎——费城交响乐团从破产中大幅复兴的广为人知案例只是最近一例——古典音乐爱好者和理论家们正在思考，这种艺术形式如何能在不牺牲其完整性的情况下融入21世纪的文化结构。

paragraphs.text: For example, should we feel OK "clapping" during classical music events, even if nobody else is? Why shouldn't we cheer for something great, like we do at a rock concert? The Huffington Post recently ran a Great Debate on this issue and many commenters came out on the side of silence. "There is no more rewarding experience in life than being part of an audience where everybody is leaning forward in silence, thoroughly carried away by a great performance of a masterpiece," one commenter wrote. "Why is it so difficult for folks to develop an appreciation and understanding for the mannerisms and traditions of classical music?" asked another.
paragraphs.translation: 例如，我们是否应该觉得在古典音乐活动期间“鼓掌”是可以的，即使其他人都没鼓掌？为什么我们不应该为精彩之处欢呼，就像在摇滚音乐会上那样？《赫芬顿邮报》最近就这个问题进行了一场大辩论，许多评论者都支持保持沉默。“生活中没有什么比成为观众的一员更令人满足的体验了，所有人都在寂静中身体前倾，完全沉浸在一部杰作的精彩表演中，”一位评论者写道。“为什么人们如此难以培养对古典音乐的风格和传统的欣赏和理解呢？”另一位评论者问道。

paragraphs.text: The truth is that classical music audiences weren't always so polite. Robert Greenberg, an award-winning composer, said that when Beethoven first performed his 7th Symphony, audiences forced the orchestra to perform encores (重演) of certain movements immediately, applauding wildly. And in the last few decades, he said, many audiences at opera performances have abandoned pretenses, yelling "Bravo" when they feel like it.
paragraphs.translation: 事实是，古典音乐观众并非总是如此有礼貌。获奖作曲家罗伯特·格林伯格说，当贝多芬首次演奏他的第七交响曲时，观众们强行要求乐团立即重演（重演）某些乐章，并热烈鼓掌。他说，在过去几十年里，许多歌剧表演的观众也抛弃了做作，想喊“Bravo”时就喊出来。

paragraphs.text: "I don't think there's anything wrong with an audience showing their enthusiasm for a proper moment by applauding, showing their joy," Greenberg said, noting that the stuffiness in concert halls is "one aspect of contemporary concert etiquette" he doesn't understand. "Instead of waiting half an hour to show enthusiasm, why not show it every eight or nine minutes?"
paragraphs.translation: “我认为观众在适当的时刻通过鼓掌来表达对音乐的热情，展示他们的喜悦，这没什么不对，”格林伯格说，并指出音乐厅里的拘谨是他不理解的“当代音乐会礼仪的一个方面”。“与其等半小时才表达热情，为什么不在每八九分钟就表达一次呢？”

paragraphs.text: Until the rules about behavior and clothing change, it's hard to imagine multitudes of young people filling concert halls on their own accord. They're probably more likely to head to Central Park to watch a free performance with a bottle of wine and their friends. "I think anyone should be able to come into a performance dressed any way they like, and be comfortable any way they like, sitting in that seat ready to enjoy themselves," Greenberg said. "Because it's enjoyable."
paragraphs.translation: 除非关于行为和着装的规则改变，否则很难想象大量年轻人会自愿涌满音乐厅。他们更可能带着一瓶酒和朋友们去中央公园观看免费演出。“我认为任何人进入演出场所时都可以穿任何他们喜欢的衣服，以任何他们喜欢的方式感到舒适，坐在座位上准备享受自己，”格林伯格说。“因为这是享受。”

paragraphs.text: Greenberg stressed that he doesn't want people to start respecting the music less, and he's not suggesting that we "dumb down" the experience. Rather, it's about opening up "access". When operas first instituted subtitles (字幕) during shows, he said, many purists didn't like the idea, believing that the audience should instead study the works before attending. But now it's commonplace to find titles on the seatback in front of you—choose a language, sit back, and understand what's going on.
paragraphs.translation: 格林伯格强调，他并非希望人们开始减少对音乐的尊重，他也不是建议我们“降低”体验的标准。相反，这是关于开放“准入”途径。他说，当歌剧在演出中首次引入字幕时，许多纯粹主义者不喜欢这个主意，认为观众应该事先研究作品。但现在，发现你前面的座椅靠背上就有字幕（可选择语言）已是司空见惯——坐回去，就能理解发生了什么。

paragraphs.text: Allison Vulgamore, president of the Philadelphia Orchestra, is certainly looking to the future. She says certain "classics concerts" dedicated to the old masters will always exist, but not every program has to feature Beethoven and Brahms—or even a stage and seats. "We're trying to introduce different kinds of concerts in different ways," she said. "We are an interactive society now, where people like to learn."
paragraphs.translation: 费城交响乐团总裁艾莉森·瓦尔加莫尔无疑在展望未来。她说，某些致力于古典大师的“经典音乐会”将永远存在，但并非每个节目都必须有贝多芬和勃拉姆斯——甚至不一定需要舞台和座位。“我们正试图以不同的方式引入不同种类的音乐会，”她说。“我们现在是一个互动社会，人们喜欢学习。”

paragraphs.text: As the Philadelphia Orchestra rebounds from its financial straits, it is also aiming to experiment, without alienating the loyalists. Vulgamore pointed to Cirque de la Symphonic, a recent offering in which jugglers (玩杂耍的人) and acrobats (杂技演员) interacted with musicians. An upcoming collaboration with New York City's Ridge Theatre, meanwhile, will feature a "suspended dance installation" and other theatrical elements occurring in conjunction with an orchestral piece.
paragraphs.translation: 随着费城交响乐团从财务困境中复兴，它也旨在进行实验，同时不疏远忠实支持者。瓦尔加莫尔提到了最近的一场演出“交响马戏团”，其中玩杂耍的人（玩杂耍的人）和杂技演员（杂技演员）与音乐家互动。与此同时，即将与纽约市里奇剧院的合作将包含一个“悬浮舞蹈装置”以及其他与管弦乐作品结合的戏剧元素。

paragraphs.text: The orchestra also continues to offer $25 annual memberships to Philadelphia students, who can buy rush tickets to every concert on the schedule. "Students line up for the concerts they want, and we get roughly 300 or 350 kids a night coming to these. They take any of the open seats available, 5 minutes before the concert starts," Vulgamore said. "It's like the running of the bulls, that energy when the doors open."
paragraphs.translation: 该乐团还继续向费城的学生提供25美元的年费会员资格，他们可以购买日程表上每场音乐会的折扣票。“学生们排队购买他们想要的音乐会门票，每晚大约有300或350名学生前来观看。他们在音乐会开始前5分钟随便坐任何可用的空位，”瓦尔加莫尔说。“就像奔牛节一样，门打开时的那种能量。”

paragraphs.text: Greenberg thinks that youthful energy needs to be harvested. Conductors don't have to be arrogant and untouchable- they can be accessible. Perhaps there could even be a "bit of humor" about them, he suggested, and an abandoning of pretension within the high-art institutions themselves. "On one hand, these organizations are all saying the same thing: we want more general audiences, to break down cultural barriers," he said. "But then they come up with some very snooty (目中无人的) thing that makes you crazy."
paragraphs.translation: 格林伯格认为这种青春活力需要被引导。指挥家不必傲慢且难以接近——他们可以平易近人。他建议，也许他们甚至可以带点“幽默感”，并且高雅艺术机构本身也要摒弃装腔作势。“一方面，所有这些机构都在说同一件事：我们想要更多普通观众，打破文化障碍，”他说。“但接着他们又会做出一些非常目中无人（目中无人的）的事情，让人抓狂。”

paragraphs.text: John Terauds, a critic who has covered Toronto's classical music scene extensively, also wants to do away with the stuffiness. He suggested that the warmer an audience is, the better the musicians themselves will respond. "But the producer or organizer has to let everyone know it's OK," he said. "It's OK to enjoy yourself." At the Toronto Symphony Orchestra, for example, conductor Peter Oundjian often stops between pieces, taking a moment to talk about the composer or the music in a very amiable way. And some nights, Terauds said, "at least a third" of the audience consists of students who have purchased cheaper tickets. On these nights, the energy of the room drastically shifts. It becomes a less intimidating place.
paragraphs.translation: 约翰·特劳兹是一位广泛报道多伦多古典音乐界的评论家，他也希望摒弃拘谨。他建议说，观众越热情，音乐家本身的表现就越好。“但制作人或组织者必须让大家知道这没关系，”他说。“享受自己没关系。”例如，在多伦多交响乐团，指挥家彼得·昂德吉安经常在曲目之间停顿一下，以非常亲切的方式谈论作曲家或音乐。特劳兹说，有些晚上，“至少三分之一”的观众是购买了便宜门票的学生。在这些晚上，整个房间的氛围会发生巨大变化。它变得不那么令人生畏。

paragraphs.text: Back in February, Terauds wrote on his blog about how going to classical performances can be intimidating. Certain people "think they have to dress up," he wrote. "They think they have to know something about the music before they go. And, I'm sure, sitting in a seat, trembling in fear that this might be the wrong time to applaud, is also one of the factors."
paragraphs.translation: 今年早些时候，特劳兹在博客上写道，参加古典音乐演出可能会让人望而生畏。他写道，有些人“认为他们必须盛装打扮”。“他们认为在去之前必须了解一些音乐知识。而且，我敢肯定，坐在座位上，为这可能是鼓掌的错误时机而颤抖，也是因素之一。”

paragraphs.text: Everyone in the classical world agrees on the need for increased "accessibility," but achieving it is often easier said than done. Nowadays, there are unknown, unorthodox opera singers wowing (博得...的喝彩) viewers on TV programs like "America's Got Talent" and "The Voice". What can higher institutions do with any of that? And if they appeal to these outlets, do they risk compromising the integrity or the intelligence of the music?
paragraphs.translation: 古典音乐界所有人都认同增加“可及性”的必要性，但实现这一点往往说起来容易做起来难。如今，有不知名、非正统的歌剧演唱家在《美国达人秀》和《美国好声音》等电视节目上赢得观众喝彩（博得...的喝彩）。高等机构能对此做什么呢？如果他们求助于这些平台，是否会危及音乐的完整性或艺术性？

paragraphs.text: Vulgamore seems to understand this. She thinks an organization can have it both ways, claiming the new while keeping the old. And as she reorganizes the Philadelphia Orchestra, she will attempt to do just that. "The world's most respected musicians brought together as an orchestra will always exist," she said. "But it's essential that we be willing to experiment and fail."
paragraphs.translation: 瓦尔加莫尔似乎理解这一点。她认为一个机构可以两者兼得，在保持传统的同时拥抱创新。在她重组费城交响乐团的过程中，她将尝试这样做。“世界上最受尊敬的音乐家组成的乐团将永远存在，”她说。“但至关重要的是，我们要愿意尝试并接受失败。”

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: How can one person enjoy good health, while another person looks old before her time? Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles. Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves. Some lifestyle factors may even turn genes on or shut them off.
paragraphs.translation: 为什么一个人能享受健康，而另一个人却未老先衰？人类数千年来一直在问这个问题，最近，科学家越来越清楚，人们衰老速度的差异在于基因、社会关系、环境和生活方式之间的复杂相互作用。尽管你出生时带有一组特定的基因，但你的生活方式会影响它们的表达方式。一些生活方式因素甚至可能开启或关闭基因。

paragraphs.text: Deep within the genetic heart of all our cells are telomeres, or repeating segments of noncoding DNA that live at the ends of the chromosomes (染色体). They form caps at the ends of the chromosomes and keep the genetic material together. Shortening with each cell division, they help determine how fast a cell ages. When they become too short, the cell stops dividing altogether. This isn't the only reason a cell can age—there are other stresses on cells we don't yet understand very well, but short telomeres are one of the major reasons human cells grow old. We've devoted most of our careers to studying telomeres, and one extraordinary discovery from our labs is that telomeres can actually lengthen.
paragraphs.translation: 在我们所有细胞的遗传核心深处是端粒，即位于染色体末端的重复非编码DNA片段。它们在染色体末端形成帽子，将遗传物质保持在一起。随着每次细胞分裂而缩短，它们帮助决定细胞衰老的速度。当它们变得太短时，细胞就完全停止分裂。这不是细胞衰老的唯一原因——我们对细胞的其他压力还不甚了解，但短端粒是人类细胞变老的主要原因之一。我们职业生涯的大部分时间都致力于研究端粒，我们实验室的一个非凡发现是端粒实际上可以变长。

paragraphs.text: Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility. Cynical hostility is defined by high anger and frequent thoughts that other people cannot be trusted. Someone with hostility doesn't just think, "I hate to stand in long lines"; they think, "Others deliberately sped up and beat me to my rightful position in the line!" and then get violently agitated. People who score high on measures of cynical hostility tend to get more heart disease, metabolic disease and often die at younger ages. They also have shorter telomeres. In a study of British civil servants, men who scored high on measures of cynical hostility had shorter telomeres than men whose hostility scores were low. The most hostile men were 30% more likely to have short telomeres.
paragraphs.translation: 科学家发现，几种思维模式似乎对端粒有害，其中之一是愤世嫉俗的敌意。愤世嫉俗的敌意被定义为高度愤怒和经常认为他人不可信任。有敌意的人不仅仅是想，“我讨厌排长队”；他们会想，“其他人故意加速，抢走了我在队伍中的正当位置！”然后变得极度激动。在愤世嫉俗敌意测量中得分高的人往往更容易患上心脏病、代谢疾病，并且通常在更年轻时死亡。他们的端粒也更短。在一项对英国公务员的研究中，在愤世嫉俗敌意测量中得分高的男性比敌意得分低的男性端粒更短。最具敌意的男性拥有短端粒的可能性高出30%。

paragraphs.text: What this means: aging is a dynamic process that could possibly be accelerated or slowed—and, in some aspects, even reversed. To an extent, it has surprised us and the rest of the scientific community that telomeres do not simply carry out the commands issued by your genetic code. Your telomeres are listening to you. The foods you eat, your response to challenges, the amount of exercise you get, and many other factors appear to influence your telomeres and can prevent premature aging at the cellular level. One of the keys to enjoying good health is simply doing your part to foster healthy cell renewal.
paragraphs.translation: 这意味着：衰老是一个动态过程，可能被加速或减缓——在某些方面甚至可以逆转。在某种程度上，端粒并不简单地执行遗传密码发出的指令，这让我们和科学界其他人士感到惊讶。你的端粒正在倾听你。你吃的食物、你对挑战的反应、你获得的运动量以及许多其他因素似乎都会影响你的端粒，并可以在细胞水平上防止过早衰老。享受健康的关键之一就是尽你所能促进健康的细胞更新。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Scientists have created by accident an enzyme (酶) that breaks down plastic drinks bottles. The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles.
paragraphs.translation: 科学家意外创造了一种能分解塑料饮料瓶的酶。这一突破可能通过首次实现瓶子的完全回收，帮助解决全球塑料污染危机。

paragraphs.text: The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan. Scientists have now revealed the detailed structure of the crucial enzyme produced by the bug.
paragraphs.translation: 这项新研究源于2016年在日本一个垃圾场发现的第一种自然进化以塑料为食的细菌。科学家现已揭示了这种细菌产生的关键酶的详细结构。

paragraphs.text: An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles. "What actually turned out was we improved the enzyme, which was a bit of a shock," said head researcher Prof. McGeehan, at the University of Portsmouth, UK.
paragraphs.translation: 一个国际团队随后调整了酶以观察其进化过程，但测试显示他们意外地使这种分子在分解饮料瓶所用塑料方面表现更佳。英国朴茨茅斯大学的首席研究员McGeehan教授说：“实际上我们改进了酶，这有点令人震惊。”

paragraphs.text: Currently, the enzyme takes a few days to start breaking down the plastic, far faster than the centuries it takes in the oceans, but the researchers are optimistic this can be speeded up even further and become a viable large-scale process.
paragraphs.translation: 目前，这种酶需要几天时间开始分解塑料，远快于海洋中需要几个世纪的时间，但研究人员乐观地认为，这可以进一步加速，并成为可行的大规模过程。

paragraphs.text: "What we are hoping to do is use this enzyme to turn this plastic back into its original components, so we can literally recycle it back to plastic," said McGeehan. "It means we won't need to dig up any more oil and, fundamentally, it should reduce the amount of plastic in the environment."
paragraphs.translation: McGeehan说：“我们希望用这种酶将塑料变回其原始成分，这样我们就能真正将其回收为塑料。这意味着我们不需要再开采更多石油，而且从根本上说，这应该减少环境中的塑料量。”

paragraphs.text: About 1 million plastic bottles are sold each minute around the globe and, with just 14% recycled, many end up in the oceans where they have polluted even the remotest parts, harming marine life and potentially people who eat seafood. "Plastic is incredibly resistant to degradation," said McGeehan. "It is one of these wonder materials that has been made a little bit too well."
paragraphs.translation: 全球每分钟售出约100万个塑料瓶，但只有14%被回收，许多最终进入海洋，污染了即使是最偏远的地区，危害海洋生物，并可能影响食用海鲜的人。McGeehan说：“塑料对降解极其耐受。它是一种有点过于出色的神奇材料。”

paragraphs.text: Currently those bottles that are recycled can only be turned into opaque fibres for clothing or carpets, while the new enzyme indicates a way to recycle old clear plastic bottles back into new clear plastic bottles.
paragraphs.translation: 目前，那些被回收的瓶子只能变成用于服装或地毯的不透明纤维，而这种新酶表明了一种将旧透明塑料瓶回收为新透明塑料瓶的方法。

paragraphs.text: "You are always up against the fact oil is cheap, so plastic is cheap," said McGeehan. "It is so easy for manufacturers to generate more of that stuff, rather than even try to recycle, but I believe there is a public interest here: perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles."
paragraphs.translation: McGeehan说：“你总是面临石油便宜，所以塑料也便宜的事实。制造商很容易生产更多这种东西，而不是尝试回收，但我相信这里有公众利益：观念正在迅速变化，以至于公司开始研究如何正确回收这些瓶子。”

paragraphs.text: Prof. Adisa Azapagic, at the University of Manchester in the UK, agreed the enzyme could be useful but added: "A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem- waste- at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions."
paragraphs.translation: 英国曼彻斯特大学的Adisa Azapagic教授同意这种酶可能有用，但补充说：“需要进行全面的生命周期评估，以确保该技术不会以牺牲其他问题（包括额外的温室气体排放）为代价来解决一个环境问题——废物。”

云贵高原(the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau)大部分位于云南、贵州省境内，总面积约50万平方公里，平均海拔 2 000—4 000米，是中国第四大高原。云贵高原西高东低，河流众多，形成了许多又深又陡的峡谷(canyon)。峡谷中许多地方土壤肥沃，非常有利于多种农作物生长。

云贵高原独特的自然环境造就了生物和文化的多样性。它是中国森林和矿产资源类型十分丰富的地区，也是古人类起源的重要地区。云贵高原是中国少数民族数量最多的地区，各民族都保留了自己丰富多彩的文化传统。

The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, mostly located within Yunnan and Guizhou provinces, covers an area of about 500,000 square kilometers with an average elevation of 2,000-4,000 meters, making it the fourth largest plateau in China. The plateau slopes from west to east, with numerous rivers that have carved out many deep and steep canyons. The soil in many areas of the canyons is fertile, highly conducive to the growth of a variety of crops.

The unique natural environment of the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau has fostered biodiversity and cultural diversity. It is a region in China with a rich variety of forest and mineral resources, as well as an important area for the origins of ancient humans. The plateau is home to the largest number of ethnic minorities in China, each preserving their own rich and colorful cultural traditions.
